Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.schema.grammar

Class SchemaGrammar

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.schema.grammar.SchemaGrammar
Direct Known Subclasses:
PostgresSchemaGrammar, SQLiteSchemaGrammar
public abstract class SchemaGrammar extends Object
Turns a Blueprint into SQL for one database.

Each database module extends this class. The base class sends each Command to its compile method and quotes names and values; a subclass supplies the SQL for the commands and column types its database supports. Any command or type a subclass does not handle fails with an error that names it and the grammar, instead of producing wrong SQL.

Implementation Requirements:
Methods added in later versions come with a body that refuses the command, so existing grammars keep compiling. Quoting goes through wrap(String), wrapTable(String) and literal(Object); override them, not the callers, to change quoting.

    • withoutForeignKeyConstraints

      public <T> T withoutForeignKeyConstraints(Connection connection, TransactionCallback<T> work)
      Runs work in one transaction with foreign key enforcement switched off, as Laravel's withoutForeignKeyConstraints does.
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the result
      Parameters:
      connection - the connection, never null, outside any transaction
      work - the work, never null
      Returns:
      the result of the work, may be null
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the connection is inside a transaction
      RuntimeException - any failure of the work, after the transaction is undone
      Implementation Requirements:
      The base runs the work in a transaction on the connection as is. A grammar whose database can switch enforcement off for one connection overrides it; the promise that a failure undoes the whole work holds only where schema changes are transactional.

      public void createDatabase(Connection connection, String name, String template, CopyStrategy strategy)
      Creates a database.

      connection - the connection to run on, never null

    • dropDatabaseIfExists

      public boolean dropDatabaseIfExists(Connection connection, String name, boolean force)
      Drops a database if it exists and tells whether it did.
      Parameters:
      connection - the connection to run on, never null
      name - the database name, never null
      force - true to close the sessions that use the database first
      Returns:
      true if the database existed
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the grammar does not support the command
      QueryException - if a statement fails
      Implementation Requirements:
      Runs the query of compileDatabaseExists(java.lang.String), then the statement of compileDropDatabaseIfExists(org.aristonis.diwan.database.Connection, java.lang.String, boolean), and returns the answer of the query. Another process may drop the database between the two, so a true answer is not proof that this call dropped it.

      Quotes an identifier.
      Parameters:
      name - the identifier, never null

      Implementation Requirements:
      The base uses double quotes and doubles any double quote inside the name, so the name cannot end the identifier.

    • literal

      protected String literal(Object value)
      Writes a default value as SQL.
      Parameters:
      value - the value, never null, of a type ColumnDefinition.defaultValue(Object) keeps
      Returns:
      the SQL literal, never null
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if text holds a NUL character
      Implementation Requirements:
      Text is put in single quotes with any single quote doubled; true and false become '1' and '0', as in Laravel; numbers are quoted in their plain decimal form; an Expression is written as given. A backslash is not escaped, because SQLite and PostgreSQL (with standard strings) read it as an ordinary character.

      the SQL literal, never null
      Implementation Requirements:
      The base returns 1 for true and 0 for false.
